content.comment_body: I upgraded my laptop to a 64-bit processor, but my [product_name] software won't install. I tried upgrading to [product_name] [version_no], but it requires the previous software version to be installed first. How can I solve this? Do I need to purchase the full version of [product_name] [version_no] to resolve the issue?

If you have the original CD for the software, you don't need the existing software installed; you can access the downloadable version instead. During installation, make sure to specify the location of the original CD.
Check out this page from [company_name], although it’s not available in English.
Hello, I think you're referring to this link: Without a previous version installed, how can you upgrade using the upgrade CD for [product_name]? Best regards, [user_name]
Hi [user_name], Thanks, I missed the link. Your link is in English, while mine was in German.

analysis.insight_summary: The user faced compatibility problems after moving to a 64-bit laptop, as their legacy [product_name] software wouldn't install. Upgrading to the newer version also requires the previous software to be installed, causing a frustrating situation for those who only have upgrade licenses and incompatible hardware. This affects ongoing work and highlights a usability issue when updating systems.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects an easier upgrade option that doesn't rely on having the old, incompatible software installed, hoping for a smooth process to update [product_name] to the latest version after changing hardware.
